answer: Clone keys are cheap, so admission should be a slow voyage rather than a signature. A recruit locks a bond and is assigned a hollow — a rotating peer set — and vote weight rises above dust only after eight epochs of work those peers can recompute from the log. A second persona needs another bond and wait; one copied log cannot sit in two hollows. Peers match log hashes to timestamps and slash a silent recruit. If the bond is a rounding error, a whale parks coins in empty hollows like wind on a barren dune, so the stake tracks recent emission and idle deposits burn when the window closes.
